reasoning_traces.think:
The emergence of spatial form from local signs hinges on ordered succession and qualitative gradation. Each local sign contributes to a structured whole, where the line itself becomes the organizing principle. When successive stimuli activate local signs in a consistent temporal pattern—such as along a retinal or skin axis—the resulting perceptual line reflects both physical continuity and cognitive ordering. This implies that spatial perception arises not merely from individual sensations but from the relational structure among them. The system must maintain an immutable order within a qualitative scale, ensuring that each element occupies a unique position relative to others. Failure occurs when transitions lack consistency or when qualitative differences are absent, leading to fragmented or non-spatial percepts. Thus, the core mechanism involves a dual constraint: temporal causality (successive activation) and ordinal coherence (qualitative ranking). These constraints enable GSI to model perception as a probabilistic process over ordered sequences, while GSE encodes the same dynamics through deterministic state transitions.
